Both products lie on their sides with the original front labels turned up toward the camera. Large serum occupies the right-middle, long axis angled gently from lower-left toward upper-right, its pump around x=77%, y=13% and base around x=62%, y=84%. Cream lies alongside at upper-right with its front label facing camera, no overlap blocking names. Product group fills the right 54% with strong close product scale.
[COMPOSITION]
A deliberate diagonal still life on one continuous subtly textured cool gray matte surface. Products feel casually set down after a daily ritual, grounded with real soft contact shadows, frosted glass edges and restrained brushed silver reflections. No extra props are needed. Continuous surface crosses the full width without horizon, seam or architectural edge. Keep entire pump and whole cream jar in frame.
[COMPOSITION FOR TEXT OVERLAY]
The left 40% of the real surface sits in a naturally darker charcoal-gray shadow with enough tonal calm for white HTML text added later. Fine surface texture, soft raking reflections and shadow flow visibly connect the left to the product area. Never manufacture a half-and-half layout, flat strip or separate panel.
[ATMOSPHERE]
Calm, sophisticated, precise daily skincare still life with tangible glass and metal; quiet cinematic depth.
[LIGHTING]
Directional 6000K key from upper camera-right at 45 degrees, large softbox diffusion with a controlled raking edge. Brushed-silver lids and collar hold dimensional slim highlights. Soft shadows travel toward the lower-left, darker across the left with a gentle falloff. Plausible glass refraction, restrained highlights, no chrome glare.
[LENS & CAMERA]
50mm standard lens, f/8, overhead camera, deep enough depth of field for both original product labels to remain crisp, restrained foreground microtexture.
[COLOR PALETTE]
Cool gray, charcoal, frosted glass white, brushed silver and black pump; exact original ivory labels.

Classical minimal still-life craft, sculptural beauty lighting, restrained geometric diagonal placement grounded in a real photograph. Cinematic editorial commercial photography.

No warped product label text, no garbled letters, no fake brand names, no melted typography, no doubled labels, no fictional logos. No stale stock photography aesthetic, no synthetic stock-photo look, no over-staged feeling, no unrealistically clean environments, no perfect symmetry where natural asymmetry should be, no clipart elements, no flat illustration mixed with photo, no obviously composited backgrounds.
